subject: Compensation band taxonomy & market mapping — request and next steps
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, bench@marketbench.co
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Compensation band taxonomy & market mapping — request and next steps

Hi team / MarketBench,

Following our discussion last week, attaching the latest draft of Redwood's comp-band template (comp_band_v0.3.xlsx). Goal: map our existing level definitions to an external market taxonomy and produce geo anchors for US, EU, and APAC priority markets. Key asks: 

- MarketBench: can you confirm which public comps and survey slices you will use and provide a sample snapshot by next Tuesday? Prefer salary + total cash (target) split.
- Laura: can you validate role list and flag unusual job families where leveling deviates (e.g., infra / SRE vs product engineering)?
- Marissa & Karthik: we need a headcount-impact estimate if we move to the proposed anchors (delta in comp spend for FY27).

Attached: comp_band_v0.3.xlsx (draft bands, level descriptions). I included our current bands in the second tab. I'll consolidate notes from MarketBench into a single mapping doc.

Timeline: ideally a consolidated recommendation by 11/25 so we can review with Eng leadership the week of 11/29.

Thanks —
Priyom Das
Talent Operations Lead | Redwood Inference
pri@redwood.com

Attachment: comp_band_v0.3.xlsx (Excel, 120KB)
From: MarketBench Research <bench@marketbench.co>
To: priyom.das@redwood.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Compensation band taxonomy & market mapping — request and next steps

Hi Priyom —

Thanks for the file. Quick notes from our initial pass (see attached snapshot):

- Data sources: Sourcing a blended view from public filings, private survey panels, and proprietary placements (we'll show weights).
- Markets: we'll provide band anchors for: US (SF, NY, SEA), EU (London, Berlin), APAC (Bengaluru, Singapore).
- Levels: we'll map to a four-tier external taxonomy (IC2/IC3/IC4/IC5 equivalents).

Questions for clarity before we finalize the sample: 
1) Do you want guaranteed compensation ranges (base only) or total cash medians + 25/50/75 percentiles?
2) For roles with variable compensation (sales, solution architects), should we treat OTE as separate?

We attached market_snapshot_nov2026.pdf with a short sample and our methodology. We'll produce the full band mapping by 11/24 if the scope stays the same.

Best,
Elena Moran
Senior Analyst | MarketBench Research
elena.moran@marketbench.co

Attachment: market_snapshot_nov2026.pdf (PDF, 520KB)
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: priyom.das@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: bench@marketbench.co
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 10:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Compensation band taxonomy & market mapping — request and next steps

Priyom / all —

Thanks for pulling this together. A few quick items from my side after skimming the draft: 

- The level descriptions currently conflate scope and impact in Level 3 (e.g., \"leads projects\" vs \"mentors other engineers\"). We should split scope (scope of influence) and proficiency (depth).
- For geo anchors: please keep US anchors at total cash medians but provide separate base %s — hiring managers need base clarity for offer negotiations.
- Can MarketBench include market sample size per role? Small N would change confidence.

I've attached a cleaned role file (redwood_role_list.csv) with suggested normalizations for job titles. You'll see a few role families (data infra, low-level systems) where market comps look sparse — expect wider percentiles there.

Also — we should be explicit about whether we plan to index mid-year or keep anchors fixed for FY27. My recommendation: lock anchors for the first half and review in Q3.

Laura Bennett
Head of Talent Strategy | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood_role_list.csv (CSV, 45KB)

Cc: bench@marketbench.co
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 11:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Compensation band taxonomy & market mapping — request and next steps

Quick operational note — thanks for the attachments. A couple of pickup items before we lock anchors: 

- Headcount impact (high level): if we move US anchors up to MarketBench median across the board, FY27 comp spend delta approximates +8.6% (rough sketch) — driven mostly by senior ICs in SF. I'll run a tighter model once we have finalized bands.
- Localization policy: recommend we keep offers pegged to city-level anchors for on-site roles and a regional anchor for remote hires (US national unless candidate is in high-cost city).
- Level mappings: propose the following mapping for engineering ICs:
  * RL-2 -> External IC2 (junior)
  * RL-3 -> External IC3 (mid)
  * RL-4 -> External IC4 (senior)
  * RL-5 -> External IC5 (staff)

Action items for me: run a headcount spreadsheet (scenario A: move medians; scenario B: move 75th pct) and share by 11/24 EOD.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Finance Partner, People Ops | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

Team / Elena —

Appreciate the quick turn. Karthik — thanks for the headcount delta sketch; that helps. Next steps and owners: 

- MarketBench (Elena): finalize the band mapping PDF and include per-role sample N by 11/25 EOD (Attachment: CompBand_Mapping_Proposal.pdf).
- Karthik: send the two scenario spreadsheets (median vs 75th) and include fiscal impact + headcount-run rate by 11/26 EOD.
- Laura: confirm whether Talent will recommend a Q3 review cadence or a mid-year index.
- Marissa: prepare a short note for Hiring Managers with negotiation guardrails (base %, sign-on guidance) — target draft by 11/29.

I scheduled a short sync on 11/30 9:00am PT — calendar invite sent. Please upload final artifacts to the Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD-CompBandReview and paste the HubSpot ref once available (HS-789012).

If anyone wants to push the external sample to include APAC salary banding in INR and SGD explicitly, note that in replies — MarketBench said they're happy to add it.

Thanks —
Priyom Das
Talent Operations Lead | Redwood Inference
